implemented: Poll panel distinguishes enabled polling, disabled polling, and unavailable details. Counts mean question results for districts. Methods and district details start collapsed; source links and reported or missing sample sizes are visible on expansion.

The map, race detail and polling picker share district selection. The mobile polling picker retains focus without jumping to the sidebar. Model changes replace the associated polling facts. District exclusions initially show ten records, with an expansion button.

Plain language explains the 100-day fieldwork-end window, question/sample/pollster deduplication, estimated availability, conditional two-candidate shares, shared errors and the absence of an additional sample-size weight.

The website collection uses HouseLiveSitePollingDisclosureV1, distinct from backend HouseLivePollingDisclosureV1. The browser parser binds run and result hashes, cutoffs, admission evidence, source identity, district counts and safe URLs, and returns independent copies.

The offline importer accepts an explicit polling directory and receipt/ledger pins. It derives the website artifact from authenticated native policy, admission and all 16 result identities. Raw receipt and ledger files stay offline; native evidence remains unchanged.

The reviewed selector implementation hash identifies the explained ruleset. Exact question IDs and candidate pairs must match the native forecast. One bare-domain KOB citation receives a narrowly checked https prefix in the derived output; the original record is unchanged.

For exclusions without a current district, unused pollster names and dates stay offline. The browser receives no raw poll percentages, respondent identities, publisher-name lists or source filesystem paths.

remaining: No current House release was imported or deployed. All 16 qualified native results, the catalog, numerical review and completed combined output remain prerequisites for the actual release.

The actual release should supply all five polling CLI flags: --polling-root, --polling-receipt, --polling-receipt-sha256, --polling-ledger and --polling-ledger-sha256. Optional absence supports existing releases with explicit unavailable text; it does not satisfy the requested explanations.

The backend polling disclosure is preserved as native evidence. The website artifact derives from the same pinned ledger and admission; the offline ledger supplies district-specific exclusion reasons beyond the backend’s global totals.
Only derived selection facts and citations enter the browser. Raw third-party source datasets remain offline.

The standing goal still requires qualified full-stack complementarity, weakest-layer identification and continuing model improvements. No scientific model run or promotion occurred here. Saving user configurations remains outside scope.
